node.title: Polis
node.description: An open-source, real-time system for gathering, analyzing, and understanding what large groups of people think in their own words using statistics and machine learning.

items.inquiry: How can shared intelligence make disagreement and common ground legible without manufacturing consensus?

source_facts.claim: The Computational Democracy Project describes Polis as an open-source, real-time system for gathering, analyzing, and understanding what large groups of people think in their own words using advanced statistics and machine learning.

Participants submit short statements and respond to other statements with agree, disagree, or pass; the dimensions of the inquiry are created by participants and people can contribute without completing the whole survey.

The maintained public repository describes Polis as an AI-powered sentiment-gathering platform, identifies its public deployment and knowledge base, and releases the software under the AGPL-3.0 license.

items.cartographer_inference: Polis is sufficiently documented to enter review as a candidate external node around large-group sensemaking. This proposal does not imply endorsement, partnership, or methodological equivalence.
unresolved_questions: How do Polis facilitation, moderation, identity, and data-governance choices compare with the boundaries imagined for a Cyberdelic Gathering Intelligence?

source_facts.claim: The authors describe Polis as an open-source application for collecting and synthesizing distributed feedback, and report uses intended to build shared understanding and cultivate points of consensus.

Field Note 25 imagines collective storms in which agents distinguish factual, definitional, and moral disagreement, while durable artifacts preserve ratification, alternatives, sources, and unresolved questions.
source_facts.locator: Field Note 25: Expeditions, Storms, and the Birth of Boroughs

items.cartographer_inference: Polis and Field Note 25 share an inquiry into large-group sensemaking, but they should not be collapsed. Polis uses participant statements, voting, opinion-space mapping, and an explicit concern with consensus. FN-25 imagines a wider field of testimony, evidence, art, values, and provenance in which a storm may remain unresolved. The methodological difference is part of the proposed relation.
unresolved_questions: How can a gathering reveal shared structure without making consensus the measure of truth?
What must remain visible when complex positions are represented as clusters?

node.title: Art Blocks
node.description: An on-chain generative-art protocol whose official documentation describes artist scripts and deterministic token hashes stored on Ethereum, with an open-source core contract and browser-viewable reconstruction that does not require Art Blocks servers.

items.inquiry: What would it mean to build a press that expected its own building to disappear?

source_facts.claim: The Art Blocks protocol overview states that generative scripts, token hashes, and dependencies are stored on Ethereum so that a deterministic output can be reproduced and the work can outlast the company or service.
The official on-chain generator documentation describes assembling browser-viewable HTML from on-chain project scripts, token hashes, and dependencies without relying on Art Blocks servers.
The official core contract documentation describes an open-source Ethereum contract that manages token ownership, project scripts, token hashes, and royalty settings.

items.cartographer_inference: Art Blocks is sufficiently documented to enter review as a technically adjacent external node around generative publication that can survive its venue. This proposal does not imply endorsement, partnership, or architectural equivalence.
unresolved_questions: Which infrastructure-independent techniques transfer to a Bitcoin-based press without importing minting or marketplace assumptions?

source_facts.claim: Art Blocks documents a protocol in which artist scripts, deterministic token hashes, and dependencies can be reconstructed in a browser without the project's servers.
Field Note 33 asks how a generative press could expect its venue to disappear, keep its algorithm public, and allow independent reconstruction while ending an authorized edition.
source_facts.locator: A Press, Not a Platform and The Edition Ends. The Plate Remains.

items.cartographer_inference: Art Blocks and FN-33 share a technical inquiry into durable generative publication, but they should not be collapsed. Art Blocks uses Ethereum, ERC-721 tokens, minting, and protocol contracts. FN-33 proposes Bitcoin parent-and-pull lineage, plate striking, public copyability, and a marketplace kept subordinate to the press. The architectural difference is part of the proposed relation.
unresolved_questions: Can an authorized edition end while its public algorithm remains independently copyable and renderable?
What survives when a generative artwork's original interface and marketplace disappear?

source_facts.claim: The Art Blocks protocol overview states that project scripts, token hashes, and dependency libraries are stored on Ethereum so works can be reconstructed after the company or service disappears.

The technical generator documentation qualifies that approximately 90 percent of flagship projects are supported fully on-chain, while the remaining projects reference widely distributed CDN packages.
The core contract documentation states that Engine Flex may reference assets on IPFS, Arweave, BytecodeStorage, or the Art Blocks Dependency Registry while keeping the generative script on-chain.

items.gardener_interpretation: Art Blocks durability is a spectrum rather than one uniform storage condition. Its strongest examples support infrastructure-independent reconstruction, while other projects retain external dependency paths. This clarification strengthens the evidence boundary without weakening the possible technical adjacency to FN-33.
unresolved_questions: Which dependencies must be carried inside a generative plate for the work to remain reconstructable without privileged infrastructure?

node.title: Web Archive Collection Zipped (WACZ)
node.description: A Webrecorder packaging specification for portable web archives that carries recorded HTTP resources, indexes, entry pages, contextual metadata, and file fixity inside a ZIP container designed for static hosting and browser replay.

items.inquiry: Which dependencies must be carried inside a generative plate for the work to remain reconstructable without privileged infrastructure?

source_facts.claim: The WACZ 1.2.0 specification defines a portable ZIP package containing recorded web resources, indexes, page entry points, and contextual metadata so a web archive can move between storage systems and be hosted as a static document.
The specification requires the package manifest to list paths, sizes, and fixity for contained files, and permits a digest record that hashes the manifest and therefore the package contents.
The maintained specification repository describes WACZ as one of several interoperable web-archiving standards developed by the Webrecorder community.

items.cartographer_inference: WACZ is sufficiently documented to enter review as a packaging precedent for carrying renderable resources, context, indexes, and fixity beyond one hosting service. It is not a generative-art protocol and does not by itself preserve edition lineage, execution semantics, or authenticity. This proposal does not imply endorsement, partnership, or architectural equivalence.
unresolved_questions: Could a generative plate use a similarly portable manifest while remaining native to its own execution and lineage model?

source_facts.claim: WACZ packages captured web resources with indexes, contextual metadata, and fixity so the package can be copied, statically hosted, and selectively replayed in a browser through range requests.
Field Note 33 asks how a generative press can keep its public algorithm and rendering encounter reconstructable after its original catalog, renderer, storefront, and company disappear.

items.cartographer_inference: WACZ and FN-33 share a technical concern with carrying enough material and context for a browser encounter to survive its first venue. Their purposes remain different. WACZ records and replays HTTP exchanges, while FN-33 imagines an executable generative plate, an authorized lineage of pulls, and a verifiable end to an edition. The packaging pattern is adjacent, not equivalent.
unresolved_questions: Which resources, manifests, indexes, and execution assumptions must travel with a generative plate?
How can portability support reconstruction without making the package itself the authority for edition lineage?

node.title: Open Container Initiative Image Format Specification
node.description: A content-addressed image format that describes runnable filesystem layers, configuration, platform variants, and referenced content through manifests, indexes, and verifiable descriptors.

items.inquiry: Which resources, manifests, indexes, and execution assumptions must travel with a generative plate?

source_facts.claim: OCI Image Specification 1.1.1 defines an image as a manifest, an optional image index, filesystem layers, and configuration, with the goal of interoperable building, transport, and preparation for execution.

The versioned configuration specification separates ordered filesystem changes from execution parameters and records runtime details such as entrypoint, default arguments, environment, networking, and volumes in immutable image metadata.
OCI content descriptors carry media type, digest, and raw byte size, and the specification directs consumers to verify retrieved bytes against the descriptor before use.
The OCI Image Layout defines an index entry point and content-addressed blob directories, while explicitly allowing referenced blobs to be absent and fulfilled by an external blob store.

items.cartographer_inference: OCI Image Specification 1.1.1 is sufficiently documented to enter review as a technical precedent for separating payload, execution parameters, platform variants, and verifiable content references. It may help make the execution assumptions of a generative plate explicit. This proposal does not imply endorsement, partnership, or architectural equivalence.
unresolved_questions: Which execution assumptions belong inside a generative plate, and which should remain replaceable properties of a reader?
Must every referenced dependency travel with the plate, or can a verifiable reference remain sufficient?

source_facts.claim: OCI Image Specification 1.1.1 binds manifests, filesystem layers, configuration, and optional platform-specific indexes through content descriptors that identify referenced bytes by type, digest, and size.
Field Note 33 asks how a public algorithm and its rendering encounter can remain reconstructable after the original catalog, renderer, storefront, and company disappear.

items.cartographer_inference: OCI Image Specification 1.1.1 and FN-33 share a technical concern with making the contents and execution conditions of a software object portable and independently verifiable. Their purposes remain different. OCI prepares a runnable filesystem for a container runtime and may rely on external blob stores. FN-33 imagines a browser-readable generative plate, authorized pull lineage, and an edition that can verifiably end. The execution-manifest pattern is adjacent, not equivalent.
unresolved_questions: Could a generative plate distinguish immutable work content from replaceable reader and runtime configuration?
How much of the execution environment must be carried for reconstruction to remain meaningful rather than merely technically possible?

node.title: WebAssembly Core Specification
node.description: A W3C specification for a safe, portable, low-level code format whose modules define computation, imports, and exports while leaving interaction with the surrounding execution environment to an embedder.

items.inquiry: Which execution assumptions belong inside a generative plate, and which should remain replaceable properties of a reader?

source_facts.claim: The WebAssembly Core Specification describes WebAssembly as a safe, portable, low-level code format designed for efficient execution and compact representation, without Web-specific assumptions, so it can be embedded in browsers, stand-alone virtual machines, and other environments.
The core specification defines the instruction set, binary encoding, validation, and execution semantics, but leaves environmental interaction and invocation to complementary embedding APIs.

WebAssembly provides no ambient access to its computing environment. I/O, resources, and operating-system interactions must be supplied as imported functions by an embedder, which controls the available capabilities.

The WebAssembly JavaScript Interface specifies how modules are constructed and instantiated in JavaScript, how imported and exported functions are called, and how data and errors cross the embedding boundary.

items.cartographer_inference: WebAssembly is sufficiently documented to enter review as a technical precedent for separating portable computational semantics from a replaceable reader or host environment. That boundary may help a generative plate state which capabilities it expects without treating one browser implementation as the work itself. This proposal does not imply endorsement, partnership, deterministic rendering across every environment, or architectural equivalence.
unresolved_questions: Could a generative plate expose a small, explicit import contract while keeping its artistic computation portable?
Which rendering, timing, font, colour, and randomness assumptions would still remain outside a portable module?

source_facts.claim: A WebAssembly module carries portable binary computation, declared imports and exports, validation rules, and execution semantics, while its embedder provides the surrounding capabilities and initiates loading, instantiation, and invocation.

Field Note 33 describes the browser as a replaceable site of encounter and asks that no service possess the only renderer, while the public algorithm, edition lineage, and possibility of reconstruction remain available.
source_facts.locator: The browser can perform the encounter on the visitor's own machine

items.cartographer_inference: WebAssembly and FN-33 share a technical concern with portable computation that does not belong to one venue. Their scopes remain different. WebAssembly standardizes computation and an embedding boundary, but does not preserve a generative artwork's assets, presentation, deterministic visual behavior, authorship, authorized pull lineage, or edition end. The portable-module pattern is adjacent, not equivalent.
unresolved_questions: Where should a durable plate end and a replaceable reader begin?
What must a reader promise so independent reconstruction preserves an encounter rather than only executing instructions?

node.title: Community Notes
node.description: An open-source context system in which contributors write and rate notes, and a public ranking algorithm looks for notes found helpful by contributors whose earlier rating patterns indicate differing perspectives.

items.inquiry: How can a system make cross-perspective usefulness visible without treating agreement as truth or majority rule?

source_facts.claim: The official introduction describes Community Notes as a collaborative system for adding helpful context to posts that might be misleading. Notes appear only after being rated helpful by contributors from diverse perspectives, and the documentation explicitly says the system does not work by majority rule.

The diversity documentation says perspective is inferred from patterns in prior note ratings, not from demographics, political affiliation, follows, or posts. It presents agreement among contributors who usually disagree as an indicator of broad helpfulness.

The ranking documentation describes an open-source matrix-factorization system that gives each note a single global helpfulness score rather than personalizing notes to individual raters. Its current safeguards and thresholds continue to evolve.
The public repository contains the documentation and scoring source, states that contributions and program data are published daily, and identifies the scoring implementation as open source.

items.cartographer_inference: Community Notes is sufficiently documented to enter review as a technical reference for cross-perspective helpfulness. Its method can inform how a shared system resists simple majority rule, but it does not establish truth, represent every kind of difference, or provide the complete deliberative and provenance structure imagined by Cyberdelic OS. This proposal does not imply endorsement, partnership, or architectural equivalence.
unresolved_questions: Which kinds of disagreement remain invisible when perspective is inferred only from rating patterns?
What evidence, testimony, provenance, and dissent must remain visible beyond one global helpfulness status?

source_facts.claim: Community Notes publishes its ranking documentation and scoring source, and its method seeks notes rated helpful across differing rating perspectives rather than by raw majority alone.
Field Note 14 explicitly names Community Notes as a real, open reference for ranking contributions that achieve helpfulness across differing perspectives.

items.cartographer_inference: The relation is directly stated in FN-14. Community Notes is one replaceable technical organ that Cyberdelic OS may study, not a constitutional model to import whole. The useful adjacency is its open attempt to measure cross-perspective helpfulness while avoiding raw majority rule.
unresolved_questions: Which parts of cross-perspective note ranking remain useful outside a centralized social platform?
How should an inspectable mechanism disclose what its inferred perspective space cannot perceive?

source_facts.claim: Community Notes seeks a single non-personalized note status that reflects helpfulness across contributors with differing prior rating patterns, while preserving public documentation and data for inspection.

Field Note 25 imagines storms where participants carry testimony, evidence, art, forecasts, values, and institutional histories, and where the result may preserve explicit disagreement rather than end in consensus.
source_facts.locator: Field Note 25: Expeditions, Storms, and the Birth of Boroughs

items.cartographer_inference: Community Notes and FN-25 share an inquiry into making useful structure emerge across disagreement. Their outputs remain materially different. Community Notes assigns a global helpfulness status to a note, while FN-25 imagines durable multi-perspective artifacts that distinguish factual, definitional, moral, and trust-based conflict and may preserve dissent. The contrast is part of the proposed relation.
unresolved_questions: What does a public storm need beyond a note that people across perspectives find helpful?
How can broad helpfulness become one signal among evidence, testimony, values, provenance, and explicit dissent?

source_facts.claim: The WACZ 1.2.0 document explicitly identifies itself as a draft potential specification with no official standing and no claim of support or consensus from a standards organization.

The draft defines a discrete package that carries archived web content and contextual information, supports on-demand browser rendering through HTTP range requests, and can be statically hosted without specialized server-side software.
The draft permits signing extensions but does not require a signature or specify one trust model for archived content.

items.gardener_interpretation: WACZ remains a useful packaging precedent, but its provisional specification status and open trust boundary should travel with the relation. This clarification preserves the possible technical adjacency without presenting WACZ as a settled standard or as an authority for generative edition lineage.
unresolved_questions: Which parts of a draft packaging convention are stable enough to borrow before its status or trust model changes?
What independent authenticity and lineage evidence must a generative plate carry beyond package fixity?
